clue.text: Comic hero of S&M, in essence

indicators.note: in tells us the letters S and M are placed inside the word for essence

parts.note: the pith of something is its essence or core
S and M are the two letters printed with the ampersand

explanation.surface: A comic character is said to embody sadomasochism at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: S&M looks like a lurid subject, but it simply supplies the letters S and M, which go inside PITH.
explanation.definitionFit: P.G. Wodehouse's Psmith, who insists on the silent P, is a celebrated comic hero of his school and city stories.

clue.text: Error in Nicholls novel holding devotee up

indicators.note: in a down clue up tells us the whole assembly is read from the bottom, so backwards
holding says the novel's title wraps around the word for devotee

parts.note: Us is a 2014 novel by David Nicholls
a devotee is a fan

explanation.surface: A mistake is found in a David Nicholls novel that props up a devoted reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts FAN inside US to give UFANS; 'up' then turns the whole thing over to read SNAFU.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang for a muddle or blunder, a situation gone badly wrong.

clue.text: Present Psammeadwith one friend at first

parts.note: to be present is to be in
the sand-fairy in E. Nesbit's Five Children and It is the It of the title
the Roman numeral for one is I
a friend is an ally

explanation.surface: Someone gives Nesbit's sand-fairy a gift along with a companion, at the start of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Psammead is the magical creature of E. Nesbit's children's book Five Children and It, so it stands for IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean at the beginning, before things changed.

clue.text: Tailor taken for a ride outside yard

indicators.note: outside says the phrase for being duped is placed around the abbreviation for yard

parts.note: to be taken for a ride is to be had on, that is fooled

explanation.surface: A tailor is swindled while standing outside a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tailor in le Carré's Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy is Bill Haydon; HAD ON is split as HA...DON around Y.
explanation.definitionFit: In le Carré's novel the mole's codename list makes Bill Haydon the Tailor.

clue.text: Captain who chronicled famousbattle

definitions.meaning: Agatha Christie's Captain Arthur ... narrates many of Poirot's cases
the Norman victory of 1066 is the best-known battle in English history

explanation.surface: A soldier writes up a celebrated fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poirot narrator and the 1066 battle share the same name, taken from the Sussex town.

clue.text: Core audience securing opportunity for Shaw play

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
a break is a chance or opportunity
a theatre audience is the house

explanation.surface: A theatre's loyal audience gets the chance to see a Shaw play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' only says the audience gets the opportunity; the three pieces run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak House is a 1919 play by George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Word game that is supported by the masses

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of and is held up by the second

parts.note: sc. abbreviates Latin scilicet, meaning namely or that is
the rabble are the common masses

explanation.surface: A word game that has popular backing.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, short for scilicet, is used in footnotes for 'that is to say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the board game of building words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Final stage role in Othello filled by maiden

indicators.note: filled by says the villain's name has the maiden letter put inside it

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello
M abbreviates maiden, an over with no runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An actor's last role, Iago in Othello, is taken by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards, where a maiden over is one with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the adult insect, the last stage of its metamorphosis.

clue.text: Hardy treefor student of Plath

definitions.meaning: Thomas Hardy's novel Under the ... Tree names this kind of woodland
Esther, the college student narrating Sylvia Plath's The Bell Jar, bears this surname

explanation.surface: A tree from Hardy's fiction suits someone studying Sylvia Plath.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's title tree stands in a leafy forest, and Plath's heroine is Esther of that surname.

clue.text: Story of navy raft I twice deployed

indicators.note: deployed suggests the letters are moved into a new position, as troops are

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: twice says the letter I is used two times

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval tale about a raft I sent out twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges NAVY, RAFT and two I's (from 'I twice') into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's Vanity Fair is a novel, so a story in the clue's sense.

clue.text: A Brontë cover not showingits final murder victim

indicators.note: not showing its final says the last letter of the pen name is dropped

parts.note: the Brontë sisters wrote under the cover of the pseudonym Bell

explanation.surface: A Brontë pen name, hiding an ending, conceals a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: The sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; A + BEL(L) gives the brother Cain killed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel is slain by his brother Cain, the first murder.

clue.text: Stopthat short, prettything gettingall of Proust

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive person or thing
tout is French for all, the language Proust wrote in

explanation.surface: Telling someone to quit reading the whole of Proust to a pretty companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CUTIE to CUTI; 'of Proust' signals French, where tout means all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal order to cease doing something at once.

clue.text: Coffee and cocoa, say, for family close to Paddington

definitions.meaning: coffee and cocoa are examples of brown shades
the family who adopt Paddington Bear are Mr and Mrs Brown and their children

explanation.surface: Hot drinks are served to a family near Paddington station.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee and cocoa are colours in the brown range, and Paddington lives with a family of that name.

clue.text: Hero's line after part of wedding?

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for line behind the wedding vow

parts.note: I do is the vow spoken at a wedding

explanation.surface: A romantic hero's speech follows the wedding vows.
explanation.walkthrough: The vow 'I do' gives IDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is someone admired and looked up to, like a worshipped figure.

clue.text: Slippingin occasional revolutionary aspect of TheThree Musketeers

indicators.note: in places the word for slipping inside the turned-round word
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: occasional means odd, as in an odd job
slipping is erring, making mistakes

explanation.surface: A rare revolutionary streak slips into Dumas's swashbuckling tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns ODD into DDO, and 'in' puts ERRING inside it to give D-ERRING-DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is daring heroic action, the swordplay at the heart of Dumas's novel.

clue.text: Perhaps reading opposite of Misery's narrative

parts.note: reading is one of the three Rs, so R
the opposite of misery is elation

explanation.surface: A reader takes up the counterpart to Stephen King's Misery.
explanation.walkthrough: Misery is also a Stephen King novel, which makes it look like a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is an account or telling of events, a story.

clue.text: Boy from St Petersburg watched you earlier in adaptation of Mort

indicators.note: in places the two inner pieces inside the rearranged name
an adaptation reworks the original, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: watched is saw
ye is the older form of you

explanation.surface: A boy from a Russian city watched you before in a stage version of Mort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation of' turns MORT into TOM R, and 'in' places SAW and YE between. St Petersburg here is Twain's Missouri town, not Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's Tom Sawyer grows up in the fictional town of St Petersburg on the Mississippi.

clue.text: Run into recent description of Papillon

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for run goes inside the other word

parts.note: topical means current or recent
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Running into a recent review of the film Papillon.
explanation.walkthrough: Papillon is the memoir of escape from the penal colony of French Guiana.
explanation.definitionFit: Papillon's story unfolds in hot equatorial jungle and penal islands.

clue.text: Site for Sir Eustace? It's not certain

parts.note: Sir Eustace Grey is a poem by George Crabbe
a site is an area

explanation.surface: Asking where Sir Eustace lives, and hearing that nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just means the site belongs to Sir Eustace, Crabbe's mad poetic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a matter that is unclear or ambiguous.

clue.text: Style marks work of Keats

parts.note: M abbreviates the German mark currency
Keats is famous for his odes

explanation.surface: Fashion distinguishes a Keats poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or fashion.

clue.text: Nations recoiled under figure such as Ozymandias?

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure

indicators.note: recoiled means sprung back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the EU is a union of nations

explanation.surface: Nations shrink back beneath a towering figure like Ozymandias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoiled' turns EU into UE, placed below STAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's Ozymandias describes a ruined sculpture of a king in the desert.

clue.text: Dance around characters in prime positions of Night Circus feature

indicators.note: around says the dance word is wrapped about the selected letters

parts.note: bop is to dance

parts.words: characters in prime positions of Night
parts.note: the letters in places 2, 3 and 5, the prime numbers, of night are I, G and T

explanation.surface: A dance swirls round the performers in a scene of The Night Circus.
explanation.walkthrough: The prime numbers 2, 3 and 5 pick I, G, T from NIGHT. The Night Circus is Erin Morgenstern's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The big top is the main tent of a circus.

clue.text: Chuck Klostermanfinally leaves north, travelling west

indicators.note: travelling suggests letters on the move into a new order
leaves says that letter departs from the compass word
finally picks out the last letter of the writer's surname

explanation.surface: The writer Chuck Klosterman ends up leaving the north and heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives N from Klosterman; 'leaves' takes it from NORTH, leaving ORTH; 'travelling' mixes ORTH with W.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck something is to toss or hurl it.

clue.text: Shakespeare's lady has previously gone

parts.note: hath is the old form of has
gone means away

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's lady has already left.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Hathaway was Shakespeare's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hathaway married William Shakespeare in 1582.

clue.text: Creature from Jungle Book film lostby mistake on Hollywood location

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece on top of the second
lost by says the word for film disappears from the next word

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like mist on glass
Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A creature from The Jungle Book in a film lost by mistake on a Hollywood lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but means a thin layer: MIST leaves MISTAKE, giving AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the wise wolf who leads the pack in Kipling's Jungle Book.

clue.text: Range endingin Mr Jelly

parts.note: an Aga is a British make of range cooker

indicators.note: ending in tells us to take the last letter of Mr

explanation.surface: A mountain range ends in Mr Jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used as a setting agent.

clue.text: "Friends, Romans –, lend me your ears" (Julius Caesar)

definitions.text: "Friends, Romans –, lend me your ears" (Julius Caesar)

parts.words: "Friends, Romans –, lend me your ears" (Julius Caesar)
parts.note: the missing word completes Mark Antony's funeral speech

explanation.surface: Mark Antony's famous opening line, with one word blanked.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony addresses the crowd as Friends, Romans and fellow citizens of his land.

clue.text: Journalist's book about fairytale villain

indicators.note: about says the word for book surrounds the villain

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the wolf is the villain of Red Riding Hood

explanation.surface: A journalist's book on the Big Bad Wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: TOME is split TOM...E around WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Wolfe was a pioneer of New Journalism.

clue.text: This hinders people hearing content of Pearl? Swell!

indicators.note: content of means the inside letters of the word

parts.note: to wax is to grow or swell, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims with delight at a pearl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' takes EAR from the middle of PEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up of cerumen in the canal can block sound.
